key_insight: InfantNet provides a large infant-specific benchmark, with fine-tuning improving pose estimation over models trained on adults.
clinical_relevance: Infant-specific pose and shape estimation could support developmental monitoring research, but clinical utility is not established by this abstract.
method: Collected 108,902 RGB images of infants aged 6–18 months, all annotated with 2D keypoints.
Added 3D pose and shape annotations with full SMIL parameters to 11,642 images.
Used iterative annotation, multi-view rendering, and reprojection-error filtering for label quality control.
evidence_signal: Baseline experiments report consistent improvements after InfantNet fine-tuning, particularly for 3D estimation, but the abstract provides no numerical performance metrics.
watch_item: Performance outside the 6–18-month age range and in clinical settings remains unestablished.
paper_title: InfantNet: A Large Scale Dataset for Infant Body Pose and Shape Estimation
